questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A uniform solid sphere rolls without slipping down an inclined plane making an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal. The linear acceleration of its center of mass down the incline is
questions.explanationEn: For pure rolling down an incline, $a = \frac{g\sin\theta}{1 + I/(MR^2)}$. For a solid sphere, $\frac{I}{MR^2} = \frac{2}{5}$, giving $a = \frac{g\sin\theta}{1 + 2/5} = \frac{5}{7}g\sin\theta$. Hence, option (D) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A uniform thin wire of mass $M$ is bent into a semicircle of radius $R$ lying in the upper half of the $xy$-plane centered at the origin. The distance of its center of mass from the origin is
questions.explanationEn: For a semicircular arc of radius $R$, $y_{\text{cm}} = \frac{1}{\pi R}\int_0^\pi (R\sin\theta)(R\,d\theta) = \frac{R}{\pi}[-\cos\theta]_0^\pi = \frac{2R}{\pi}$. Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: An incompressible ideal fluid of density $\rho$ flows steadily through a horizontal pipe whose cross-sectional area narrows from $A$ to $A/2$. If the fluid speed in the wider section is $v$, the pressure difference $P_1 - P_2$ between the wider and narrower sections is
questions.explanationEn: By the continuity equation, $A v = (A/2) v_2 \implies v_2 = 2v$. By Bernoulli's equation for a horizontal pipe, $P_1 - P_2 = \frac{1}{2}\rho(v_2^2 - v^2) = \frac{1}{2}\rho(4v^2 - v^2) = \frac{3}{2}\rho v^2$. Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Water rises to a height $h$ in a vertical glass capillary tube of radius $r$. If the same experiment is repeated in a glass capillary tube of radius $2r$, the height of the water column will be
questions.explanationEn: By Jurin's law, capillary rise is $h = \frac{2T\cos\theta}{\rho g r} \propto \frac{1}{r}$. Doubling the radius halves the capillary rise height to $\frac{h}{2}$. Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A uniform metal wire of Young's modulus $Y$ is stretched within its elastic limit so that the longitudinal strain is $\epsilon$. The elastic potential energy stored per unit volume of the wire is
questions.explanationEn: The elastic energy density is $u = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{stress} \times \text{strain} = \frac{1}{2}(Y\epsilon)\epsilon = \frac{1}{2}Y\epsilon^2$. Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A uniform heavy wire of length $L$, mass density $\rho$, and Young's modulus $Y$ hangs vertically from a rigid ceiling. The elongation of the wire due to its own weight is
questions.explanationEn: At distance $x$ from the free bottom end, the tension due to the hanging segment below is $T(x) = \rho A x g$, giving local strain $\frac{d(\Delta l)}{dx} = \frac{\rho g x}{Y}$. Integrating from $0$ to $L$ yields $\Delta L = \int_0^L \frac{\rho g x}{Y}\,dx = \frac{\rho g L^2}{2Y}$. Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A light horizontal cantilever beam of length $L$, breadth $b$, and thickness $d$ (Young's modulus $Y$) is clamped at one end and carries a load $W$ at the free end. If both the length $L$ and the thickness $d$ are doubled while $b$ and $W$ remain unchanged, the vertical depression at the free end changes by a factor of
questions.explanationEn: The free-end depression of a rectangular cantilever is $\delta = \frac{WL^3}{3YI_g} = \frac{4WL^3}{Y b d^3} \propto \frac{L^3}{d^3}$. When both $L$ and $d$ are doubled, $\frac{(2L)^3}{(2d)^3} = \frac{8}{8} = 1$, so the depression remains unchanged. Hence, option (C) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A particle of mass $m$ moves in a one-dimensional potential $U(x) = \frac{a}{x^2} - \frac{b}{x}$ ($x > 0$, with $a, b > 0$). The angular frequency of small oscillations about its stable equilibrium position is
questions.explanationEn: Equilibrium occurs at $U'(x_0) = -\frac{2a}{x_0^3} + \frac{b}{x_0^2} = 0 \implies x_0 = \frac{2a}{b}$. The effective spring constant is $k_{\text{eff}} = U''(x_0) = \frac{6a}{x_0^4} - \frac{2b}{x_0^3} = \frac{6a b^4}{16 a^4} - \frac{2 b^4}{8 a^3} = \frac{b^4}{8 a^3}$. Hence $\omega = \sqrt{\frac{k_{\text{eff}}}{m}} = \sqrt{\frac{b^4}{8 m a^3}}$. Hence, option (D) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Sand drops vertically at a constant mass rate $\lambda$ (in $\text{kg/s}$) onto a horizontal conveyor belt moving at a constant velocity $v$. The power required by the belt motor to maintain the constant velocity $v$ is
questions.explanationEn: The horizontal force required to accelerate the falling sand from zero horizontal speed to speed $v$ is $F = \frac{dp}{dt} = \lambda v$. The mechanical power delivered by the motor is $P = Fv = \lambda v^2$. (Half of this power, $\frac{1}{2}\lambda v^2$, becomes kinetic energy of the sand, and the other half is dissipated as heat by friction.) Hence, option (D) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A planet moves in an elliptical orbit of semi-major axis $a$ and eccentricity $e$ around a star of mass $M$. When the planet is at a distance $r = a$ from the star (at the ends of the minor axis), its orbital speed is
questions.explanationEn: From conservation of energy (vis-viva equation), $\frac{1}{2}v^2 - \frac{GM}{r} = -\frac{GM}{2a} \implies v^2 = GM\left(\frac{2}{r} - \frac{1}{a}\right)$. At $r = a$, $v^2 = GM\left(\frac{2}{a} - \frac{1}{a}\right) = \frac{GM}{a} \implies v = \sqrt{\frac{GM}{a}}$. Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Consider a uniform solid sphere of mass $M$ and radius $R$. Let $g(r)$ and $\Phi(r)$ denote the magnitude of the gravitational field and the gravitational potential (with $\Phi(\infty) = 0$) at a distance $r$ from the center. Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
optionsEn: $g(r)$ attains its maximum value at the surface $r = R$
The gravitational potential at the center is $\Phi(0) = -\frac{3GM}{2R}$
The gravitational potential is constant for $r \le R$
questions.explanationEn: For a uniform solid sphere: $g(r) = \frac{GM}{R^3}r$ for $r \le R$ (linearly increasing, A is true) and $g(r) = \frac{GM}{r^2}$ for $r \ge R$, peaking at $r = R$ (B is true). Inside, $\Phi(r) = -\frac{GM}{2R^3}(3R^2 - r^2)$, which varies with $r$ (D is false) and equals $-\frac{3GM}{2R}$ at $r = 0$ (C is true). Hence, options (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Consider a Foucault pendulum oscillating at latitude $\lambda$ on the Earth (which rotates with angular speed $\Omega$ about its axis). Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
optionsEn: The plane of oscillation precesses with angular speed $\Omega\sin\lambda$
At latitude $\lambda = 30^\circ$, the plane of oscillation completes one full rotation in $12$ hours
At the Equator ($\lambda = 0^\circ$), the plane of oscillation does not precess
At the North Pole ($\lambda = 90^\circ$), the plane of oscillation completes one full rotation in one sidereal day
questions.explanationEn: The precession angular speed of a Foucault pendulum is $\omega_p = \Omega\sin\lambda$ (A is true), with period $T_p = \frac{T_{\text{sidereal}}}{\sin\lambda}$. At $\lambda = 90^\circ$, $T_p = T_{\text{sidereal}}$ (B is true). At $\lambda = 0^\circ$, $\omega_p = 0$ (C is true). At $\lambda = 30^\circ$, $T_p = \frac{24\text{ h}}{\sin 30^\circ} = 48\text{ h} \neq 12\text{ h}$ (D is false). Hence, options (A), (C), and (D) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: For a homogeneous isotropic linear elastic solid with Young's modulus $Y$, bulk modulus $K$, shear modulus $\eta$, and Poisson's ratio $\sigma$, which of the following relation(s) is/are valid?
questions.explanationEn: (A) $Y = 2\eta(1 + \sigma)$ and (C) $Y = 3K(1 - 2\sigma)$ are standard identities. Equating them gives $2\eta(1 + \sigma) = 3K(1 - 2\sigma) \implies \sigma(6K + 2\eta) = 3K - 2\eta \implies \sigma = \frac{3K - 2\eta}{6K + 2\eta}$ (C is true). For $\sigma \to 0.5$, $Y = 2\eta(1.5) = 3\eta \neq 2\eta$ (D is false). Hence, options (A), (C), and (D) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A planet of mass $m$ orbits a much heavier star of mass $M$ in a bound elliptical orbit with semi-major axis $a$ and eccentricity $e$ ($0 < e < 1$). Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
optionsEn: The angular momentum magnitude is $L = m\sqrt{GMa(1 - e^2)}$
The total mechanical energy of the planet is $E = -\frac{GMm}{2a}$ and is independent of $e$
The orbital time period $T$ depends on $a$ and is independent of $e$
The speed of the planet is constant along the elliptical orbit
questions.explanationEn: For a Keplerian ellipse: $E = -\frac{GMm}{2a}$ (A is true), $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{a^3}{GM}}$ (independent of $e$, B is true), and the semi-latus rectum $\ell = a(1 - e^2) = \frac{L^2}{GMm^2} \implies L = m\sqrt{GMa(1 - e^2)}$ (C is true). Since $e > 0$, the speed varies from maximum at perihelion to minimum at aphelion (D is false). Hence, options (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The excess pressure inside a spherical soap bubble of radius $2\text{ cm}$ made from a soap solution of surface tension $0.03\text{ N/m}$ is ____ $\text{Pa}$. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: $\Delta P = \frac{4T}{R} = \frac{4 \times 0.03}{0.02} = 6\text{ Pa}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A ball dropped from rest from a height of $16\text{ m}$ onto a horizontal floor rebounds to a maximum height of $9\text{ m}$. The coefficient of restitution between the ball and the floor is ____. (Rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.explanationEn: The rebound height is $h_1 = e^2 h_0$, so $e = \sqrt{\frac{h_1}{h_0}} = \sqrt{\frac{9}{16}} = 0.75$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A wire is stretched by $2\text{ mm}$ under a tensile load of $40\text{ N}$ within its elastic limit. The elastic potential energy stored in the wire, in $\text{mJ}$, is ____. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: $U = \frac{1}{2}F\Delta L = \frac{1}{2}(40\text{ N})(2 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}) = 0.04\text{ J} = 40\text{ mJ}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Taking the acceleration due to gravity on Earth's surface as $g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$, the acceleration due to gravity at an altitude equal to the Earth's radius ($h = R_E$), in $\text{m/s}^2$, is ____. (Rounded off to two decimal places)

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A large open tank contains water to a depth of $5\text{ m}$. A small hole is punctured near the bottom of the tank. Taking $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$, the initial efflux speed of water from the hole, in $\text{m/s}$, is ____. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: By Torricelli's theorem, $v = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2 \times 10 \times 5} = 10\text{ m/s}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM PH Topic • Mechanics and General Properties of Matter (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A uniform solid sphere rolls without slipping along a horizontal surface at $7\text{ m/s}$ and then rolls without slipping up a rough inclined plane. Taking $g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$, the maximum vertical height reached by its center of mass before momentarily stopping, in $\text{m}$, is ____. (Rounded off to one decimal place)
questions.explanationEn: The initial total kinetic energy is $K = \frac{1}{2}Mv^2\left(1 + \frac{2}{5}\right) = \frac{7}{10}Mv^2$. Equating to $Mgh$ gives $h = \frac{7v^2}{10g} = \frac{7 \times 49}{10 \times 9.8} = 3.5\text{ m}$.
